blurb: Muscular, short-coated American terrier of English bull-and-terrier stock
description: The American Pit Bull Terrier is a medium-sized, short-haired, solidly built US breed of English bull-and-terrier descent, recognized by the UKC and ADBA.
answer: The American Pit Bull Terrier is a medium-sized, short-haired, solidly built dog developed in the United States from English bull-and-terrier ancestors. It is recognized by the United Kennel Club and the American Dog Breeders Association, but not by the American Kennel Club. Males are normally about 45 to 53 cm tall and females 43 to 50 cm, and the UKC describes the breed as strong, confident and eager to please.

body: In England, Old English Terriers and Old English Bulldogs were crossed to combine terrier gameness with bulldog strength, producing the bull and terrier. These dogs reached the United States in the mid to late 19th century and became the direct ancestors of the breed. Its history is closely tied to dog fighting, which continued in America after blood sports were banned in Britain in 1835.

The UKC recognized the breed on 10 February 1898, and the ADBA has registered it since 1909. In the early 20th century the dogs were also used as catch dogs for semi-wild cattle and hogs, for driving livestock and as family companions. The AKC's related breed became the American Staffordshire Terrier.

The breed is medium-sized with smooth, well-defined muscle, round to almond-shaped eyes, small to medium ears usually carried half prick or rose, and a tail tapering to a point. Males normally weigh about 15 to 27 kg and females 13 to 22 kg. The coat is glossy, smooth, short and stiff to the touch; many colors are accepted, but the ADBA and UKC do not recognize merle. Solid and tuxedo patterns are typical.

The UKC standard describes strength and confidence as essential characteristics and calls the breed eager to please, enthusiastic, intelligent and willing to work. The ADBA standard treats aggression toward humans as a disqualifying fault. The breed is subject to breed-specific legislation in a number of countries and cities, ranging from bans to ownership restrictions.

The UKC notes that the breed is a capable climber, so good fencing is needed. With high energy and endurance, it takes part in weight pulling, agility, flyball, lure coursing and obedience, and has worked as a search and rescue, detection and therapy dog.

The breed tends to be hardy, with an average lifespan of at least 12 years, longer than many breeds of similar size. Conditions reported in the breed include hip dysplasia, degenerative myelopathy, kneecap dislocation, demodectic mange, skin allergies, thyroid problems and congenital heart defects. Puppies are described as more susceptible to parvovirus when unvaccinated.

faq.q: Is the American Pit Bull Terrier recognized by the AKC?
faq.a: No. It is recognized by the United Kennel Club and the American Dog Breeders Association, but not by the American Kennel Club or the FCI.

faq.q: How big does an American Pit Bull Terrier get?
faq.a: Males are normally about 45 to 53 cm and 15 to 27 kg, and females about 43 to 50 cm and 13 to 22 kg.

faq.q: Is a pit bull the same as an American Staffordshire Terrier?
faq.a: They share ancestry, and the UKC registers AmStaffs as American Pit Bull Terriers. Since 2015 the ADBA treats them as separate breeds, and breeders have pursued different goals for decades.

faq.q: How long do American Pit Bull Terriers live?
faq.a: The breed is described as hardy, with an average lifespan of at least 12 years, which is longer than many dogs of similar size.
